query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) can improve the room-temperature ductility of equal-atomic NbMoTaW high-entropy alloy without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW high-entropy alloy with a single-phase BCC structure
generation.intervention: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) in liquid nitrogen for a soaking time of 120 h
generation.structural_mediator: Increased lattice distortion and residual stress
generation.mechanism: The increased lattice distortion and residual stress introduced by DCT can improve the plasticity of the alloy by reducing the difference in the movement rate of edge dislocations and screw dislocations, thereby improving the ductility of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature ductility without compromising high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance
generation.boundary: The DCT treatment should be conducted in a controlled environment with precise control over the soaking time and temperature to ensure consistent results.
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of how DCT affects the irradiation resistance of the alloy is not fully understood and requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of DCT-treated and untreated NbMoTaW alloys at room temperature and 1600 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DCT-treated alloy shows no significant improvement in room-temperature ductility compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

At present, the casting forming of HEAs is facing some problems due to their high melt viscosity, and laser additive manufacturing (AM) technology can effectively solve this problem [,,]. Laser melting deposition (LMD) technology has high energy density and complex-shape-forming ability, which can solve the problem of HEA forming and accumulate thermal stress in as-deposited alloy samples []. At the same time, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) has been gradually applied as a method to uniformly aggravate the residual stress generated by LMD, and remarkable results have been achieved [].
